content: Screening and testing for type 2 diabetes and prediabetes in adults without symptoms are essential for early detection and management. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) emphasizes the importance of identifying individuals at risk. Research, such as the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP), has demonstrated that preventing the progression from prediabetes to diabetes significantly lowers the likelihood of developing diabetes-related complications, such as damage to the retina (retinopathy) and kidney disease (nephropathy).
